about: Headline figures for the US data center water comparison brief, a follow-on to the Oct 12, 2026 brief (us-data-center-water-brief). Every entry traces to data/sources.md by source key. Values are as printed in the source unless a conversion is stated. Conversions use 1 US gallon = 3.78541 liters; billion gallons per day to billion liters per year multiplies by 365 x 3.78541 = 1,381.67.

agriculture_usgs_definition.about: Agriculture as USGS defines it: irrigation plus livestock. Derived sum from S2.
agriculture_usgs_definition.livestock_feed_note: Livestock's water footprint sits mostly in feed-crop irrigation, which USGS counts under irrigation, not livestock. The 2.00 Bgal/d livestock figure alone understates agriculture and is never used standalone in this brief.

derived_comparisons.conversion_basis: 1 Bgal/d = 1,381.67 billion liters per year. Data center figures are LBNL 2023; USGS figures are 2015. Every share is cross-year and is labeled with both years wherever it appears.

datacenter_direct_share_of_total_withdra.framing_verdict: safe only with the cross-measure label printed
datacenter_direct_share_of_total_withdra.note: Carried from the Oct 12 brief: LBNL 2023 direct consumption (66 billion liters = 17.4 billion gallons per year) divided by USGS 2015 total withdrawals (322 Bgal/d x 365). Consumption compared against withdrawals; labeled as such wherever used.

datacenter_indirect_share_of_thermoelect.note: PART-VS-WHOLE OVERLAP: data centers' indirect water is a slice of the water consumed generating electricity, the same water USGS counts as thermoelectric consumptive use. The two are never added together, and this share compares a part to a whole that contains it, across a year gap (2023 vs 2015).

datacenter_total_share_of_irrigation_con.note: Data center direct plus indirect (2023) against irrigation consumption (2015).

datacenter_total_vs_smallest_withdrawal_.framing_verdict: needs framing, used only as a labeled exhibit of why the two tables cannot be merged
datacenter_total_vs_smallest_withdrawal_.note: This mixes a consumption figure against a withdrawal table (the trap this brief exists to expose). It appears only in the withdrawals chart note, explicitly labeled as a cross-measure illustration, never as a ranking.

irrigation_to_datacenter_direct_ratio.note: Irrigation consumption (USGS 2015) vs data center direct consumption (LBNL 2023).

one_day_of_irrigation_vs_datacenter_dire.arithmetic: Irrigation consumption per day = 73.2 Bgal/d x 3.78541 = 277.1 billion liters/day. 277.1 / 66 = 4.20

one_day_of_irrigation_vs_datacenter_tota.arithmetic: Data center total consumption per day = 866 / 365 = 2.37 billion liters/day. 277.1 / 2.37 = 116.8
one_day_of_irrigation_vs_datacenter_tota.note: About four months of all US data center consumption equals one day of US irrigation consumption.

lbnl_data_center_water_2023.about: LBNL 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report (S1), US data centers, consumption only. The June 2026 LBNL update publishes no water estimates, so S1 remains the water source of record.

direct_consumption_2014_billion_liters.note: Direct consumption roughly tripled 2014 to 2023 (21.2 to 66 billion liters).

indirect_consumption_billion_liters.note: Water consumed generating the electricity data centers buy, at a national average intensity of 4.52 L/kWh for data center electricity (US grid average 4.35 L/kWh).

total_consumption_billion_liters_derived.note: Derived: direct 66 + indirect nearly 800. Equals about 229 billion gallons per year, about 0.63 Bgal/d.

measures_never_mixed.consumption: water withdrawn and not returned, mostly evaporated in cooling or taken up by crops
measures_never_mixed.note: Withdrawal and consumption are different quantities. This file keeps them in separate sections, and every derived comparison states which measure each side uses.
measures_never_mixed.withdrawal: water taken from a source; some of it is returned

usgs_consumption_2015.about: USGS Circular 1441 (S2) publishes national consumptive use for only two categories, the first national consumption estimates since 1995. No national consumption figure exists in the circular for public supply, industry, livestock, aquaculture, mining, or domestic use.

irrigation.note: 62% of irrigation's total use (withdrawals plus reclaimed wastewater), as printed in the circular.

thermoelectric_power.note: Only about 3% of thermoelectric withdrawals are consumed; most cooling water is returned.

usgs_pp1894_footnote.about: USGS Professional Paper 1894, Chapter D (S3): modeled water use for the conterminous US, water years 2010-20 averages. Corroboration only; different geography (CONUS vs national), different basis (decade modeled average vs single-year compilation), thermoelectric freshwater only. Never mixed into the Circular 1441 charts or table.

no_2020_circular.note: The quinquennial Estimated Use of Water Circular series ends at 2015 (Circular 1441). There is no 2020 Circular. The remaining five categories' post-2015 estimates were released through ScienceBase data releases, not a single citable report.

usgs_withdrawals_2015.about: USGS Circular 1441 (S2), national withdrawals by category, 2015. Data center figures do not appear in this table: LBNL publishes data center consumption only, and no honest withdrawal figure for data centers exists in these sources.

aquaculture.note: Mostly flow-through raceways that return the water after use, per the circular's category text; withdrawal rank overstates consumption.
